To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
letters to the editor vary by issue scope.
letters to the editors of metropolitan newspapers differ in the degree of distance from local context, and the tone of letters varies with the degree of distance.
the tone and style of letters to the editor are related to the scope of the issue they address.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the public sphere is enacted and experienced in a technologically mediated environment.
the question of whether letters to the editor are a form of democratic participation or whether they are a way to vent anger and frustration.
the question of whether the technological mediation of the public sphere affects the nature of public discourse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
letters to the editor are a form of public discourse that is more likely to be confrontational when the issue at hand is not local.
letters to the editor are one of the many ways in which citizens seek to enact public discourse in a mediated environment.
the public sphere, in its various manifestations, is an important part of democratic life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more distant the issue, the more likely writers are to engage in emotional appeals and the less likely they are to engage in reasoned appeals.
letters to the editor can be a useful way to understand how the public sphere is enacted through mediated discourse.
the public sphere is a complex, multilayered space that is both mediated and mediated by citizens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the public sphere is not a single space, but rather is composed of multiple, overlapping publics.
letters to the editor, like other forms of public discourse, are shaped by the context within which the discourse occurs.
letters are a useful way to understand the ways in which people seek to engage in public deliberation.
